newsitem.title: USA: MCI holders approve merger with BT.
newsitem.headline: MCI holders approve merger with BT.

text.p: MCI Communincations Corp. shareholders Wednesday voted to approve the company's $23 billion merger with British Telecommunications Plc.
At a special shareholders meeting, MCI said more than 77 percent of shares were voted in favour of the colossal merger.

The shareholder vote is one of the first major milestones on the road to winning approval for the cross-border merger, which will create a combined company known as Concert Plc with $40.6 billion in revenues.

The merger awaits regulatory approvals in Washington D.C., London and Brussels, the headquarters of the European Union. Company officials are confident the merger, announced in November 1996, is on track to close in the fall of 1997.
Wilkes Barre was chosen because it was the hometown of William McGowan, the legendary founder and former chairman of MCI, who died in June 1992.
